items.title: Protect children from sexual abuse, Raissa Child Protection Initiative urges
items.description: The Raissa Child Protection Initiative over the weekend held a community durbar at Agbeve, Sowutuom, in Accra to educate residents on child sexual abuse prevention and the need to protect children from all forms of sexual exploitation. The programme forms part of efforts by the non-governmental organisation (NGO) to raise awareness of child protection, educate parents and caregivers on their responsibilities, and encourage community members to report suspected cases of abuse to the appropriate authorities. Founder of the NGO, Ms Raissa Sambou, said protecting children from sexual abuse required the collective responsibility of parents, caregivers, traditional authorities and other members of society. She said children needed safe environments where they could speak about uncomfortable experiences without fear of blame or punishment. Madam Sambou stressed that children who experienced sexual abuse were never responsible for what happened to them and urged adults to listen to them, take their concerns seriously and seek appropriate assistance when necessary. She noted that both boys and girls could be victims of sexual abuse and called for equal protection and support for all children, regardless of their sex. She also urged parents and caregivers to educate children on body boundaries, inappropriate touching and how to seek help from trusted adults. Ms Sambou cautioned that perpetrators could be people known to or trusted by children, adding that parents needed to remain vigilant and establish safeguards to protect their children. She further called on community members not to conceal abuse to protect family relationships or reputations, stressing that the safety and welfare of children must take priority. A legal practitioner and member of the Raissa Child Protection Initiative project team, Alhaji Yussif Baba Suleman, said the 1992 Constitution of Ghana contained provisions to safeguard children’s rights, making it important for people to understand those rights and ensure they were respected. He urged the public not to shield perpetrators of sexual abuse because they were relatives, friends or people close to their families. Alhaji Suleman said offenders must face the full rigours of the law to ensure justice for victims and deter others from committing similar offences He also called on residents to report suspected cases to the appropriate authorities rather than resort to secrecy or informal settlements. The durbar highlighted the importance of community participation in preventing child sexual abuse and ensuring that affected children received the necessary protection and support. Beneficiaries of the forum thanked the organising team for the valuable information shared and hoped such programmes would be held frequently in communities across the country.

items.title: Aggrieved NDC delegates invoke curses on party executives over alleged bloated register at Atwima Kwanwoma Constituency
items.description: Some aggrieved delegates of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Atwima Kwanwoma Constituency of the Ashanti Region, who allege that their names have been removed from the party’s electoral register, have invoked curses on party executives over what they describe as their failure to address the issue. Tension is currently mounting at Twedie, where the NDC constituency elections are taking place. Some aggrieved delegates allege the names of qualified delegates have been removed from the electoral album and replaced with those of persons they consider unqualified, purportedly to favour certain candidates in the elections. The aggrieved delegates say they have repeatedly reported the matter to the party’s regional executives for resolution, but their concerns have allegedly not been addressed. They claim the failure of the executives to intervene has left them with no option but to invoke the Antoa deity, calling for spiritual retribution against anyone found culpable in the alleged manipulation. “We have poured libation and slaughtered sheep while invoking Antoa Nyamaa and other river deities to deal with those allegedly responsible for the disputed changes,” they said. Speaking to the media, one of the aggrieved delegates Gifty Kobbina she expressed frustration over the development, insisting that their sacrifices and commitment to the party should not be undermined by what they describe as an attempt to disenfranchise legitimate delegates. “We have suffered for this party, and we will not allow anyone to cheat us. We are calling on Antoa to strike anyone who has a hand in this album manipulation,”she alleged. The aggrieved delegates have warned that failure to resolve their concerns could undermine the credibility of the constituency elections and deepen divisions among party members.

items.title: France protests: Latest developments
items.description: Hundreds of protests were held in France Saturday as nationwide anger grows over the cost of living, with security forces massing to prevent a repeat of violence that marred demonstrations last week. Here are the latest developments: – ‘Calm’ in Paris – French police had arrested 135 people nationwide and seized a variety of weapons, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said, adding that, so far, “there has been no major incident”. Weapons confiscated included metal balls, lead pellets, fireworks, slingshots, steel balls, improvised weapons, a katana and airsoft weapons, he said. Paris police described the situation as “calm” at midday. – ‘Scandalous’ – Hundreds of demonstrators could be seen gathering at Porte d’Italie in Paris, where authorities have said they must begin the only authorised march. Union representative Murielle Guilbert told reporters it was “scandalous” that President Emmanuel Macron had forbidden protesters from demonstrating “where we wish to demonstrate”. “We are here today, quite obviously, because there is immense social anger in this country, and because wages have still not been increased to the level they should be,” she added. Paris police at the last minute ordered the union-organised march be moved from Bastille, in the centre, to the more remote Porte d’Italie on the southeastern rim. Unions said they reluctantly agreed. But the Yellow Vests — a loosely organised group that staged disruptive street protests against Macron eight years ago — indicated they would not comply. – Halloween protests called – One group organising Saturday’s demonstrations — the Yellow Vests — said they would hold another round of protests on October 31. Organisers called for rallies and a sit-in outside parliament and city halls nationwide, condemning the “authoritarian drift” of President Emmanuel Macron’s government and urging citizens to stand up for “public freedoms”. – Tear gas in Lyon – Police fired teargas to disperse some 150 people protesting in the southeastern city of Lyon, in an area banned to all demonstrations, an AFP journalist saw. Police fired several teargas grenades to clear the group near a university faculty and the city’s police station as part of nationwide rallies against the cost of living. Police moved in as demonstrators tried to block a road. – ‘Macron resign’ – Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched in the city of Orleans against a congress by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) party there, AFP journalists saw. The protest criticised both leading presidential candidate Le Pen and centrist Macron. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled. – Louvre, Orsay closed – The Louvre, d’Orsay, and Picasso museums, as well as the Grand Palais in Paris, were closed Saturday. The culture ministry had called on institutions to take every measure to ensure the safety of visitors and staff, and the protection of artworks. items.title: Unemployment and poverty pushed us into dangerous underground mining – Atwima Kwanwoma miners
items.description: Some youth engaged in underground mining in the Atwima Kwanwoma District of the Ashanti Region say unemployment and poverty have forced them into the dangerous activity despite the risk to their lives. According to the miners, many of them have completed senior high school and tertiary education but have been unable to secure jobs, compelling them to resort to underground mining to earn a living and support their families. In an exclusive interview, one of the miners, Kwame Asah, popularly known as Tagor, disclosed that he had been involved in underground mining in the area for more than seven years. He ventured into the activity after completing senior high school but could not further his education due to a lack of financial support. “When I completed SHS, I did not get the support to further my education. As a man, I had to leave my hometown, Ejura, and come here to work to help solve the financial problems at home,” he said. Kwame described underground mining as less destructive to natural resources than surface mining, but acknowledged that it poses significant risks to the lives of those involved. He said he would readily quit the job if another employment opportunity became available, given the constant danger of underground pits collapsing. “If there is another employment opportunity for me, honestly, I will quit this job because I could die at any time if the pit collapses,” he said. The miners have consequently appealed to the government to prioritise job creation and provide sustainable employment opportunities for young people. They believe such interventions would help reduce the number of youths turning to dangerous underground mining activities as a means of survival.

items.title: Countries with the largest armies, tanks, naval fleet and aircraft
items.description: Military strength can be measured in several ways, including the number of active personnel, tanks, military aircraft and naval vessels. A country that ranks highly in one category may occupy a lower position in another, highlighting the different priorities and capabilities of armed forces worldwide. Using 2026 data from Global Firepower, this comparison examines the 10 countries with the largest military inventories across four key categories: active military personnel, tanks, military aircraft and naval assets. Active Personnel China has the world’s largest active military force, with approximately 2.04 million personnel. India ranks second with 1.43 million, followed by the United States with about 1.33 million active personnel. North Korea and Russia are also prominent in the ranking, each with approximately 1.32 million active personnel, according to the figures provided. Their positions highlight the substantial manpower maintained by countries with different military priorities. The top 10 countries with the largest active military forces are China, with 2,035,000 personnel; India, with 1,431,000; the United States, with 1,333,030; North Korea and Russia, with 1,320,000 each; Ukraine, with 900,000; Pakistan, with 660,000; Iran, with 610,000; Ethiopia, with 503,000; and Türkiye, with 481,000. The figures cover active personnel across the armed forces but exclude reservists and paramilitary organisations. North Korea’s high ranking reflects its emphasis on preparing for a potential conflict on the Korean Peninsula. Its military structure places considerable importance on ground forces, with significant strength positioned near the Demilitarised Zone separating the country from South Korea. Japan’s 2026 defence white paper also highlights the security challenges surrounding the Korean Peninsula and the military capabilities maintained by North Korea. Tank Ranks by Country China leads the ranking of countries with the largest tank inventories, followed by Russia, while North Korea occupies third place ahead of the United States. The figures illustrate the importance several countries continue to place on land-based military operations, although the number of tanks alone does not determine the effectiveness of an armoured force. Russia has 5,870 tanks, while China follows closely with 5,630. North Korea ranks third with 4,895 tanks, ahead of the United States, which has 4,666. India occupies fifth place with 3,913 tanks, followed by Egypt with 3,620. Pakistan ranks seventh with 2,677, while Iran is eighth with 2,675. Türkiye takes ninth place with 2,284 tanks, and Vietnam rounds out the top 10 with 1,999. North Korea’s extensive tank inventory reflects its long-standing focus on conventional ground warfare. Research published by the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) indicates that the country operates a combination of older Soviet-inspired designs and newer equipment. Maintaining a large number of tanks can provide a military with substantial ground-firepower capacity. However, the age and technological sophistication of the vehicles also matter. Modern armour, targeting systems, sensors, weapons and battlefield communications can significantly affect the performance of tanks in combat. Consequently, a country with a larger inventory does not necessarily possess a more effective armoured force than one with fewer but more advanced vehicles. Military Aircraft The United States has the world’s largest military aircraft inventory, with 13,032 aircraft, placing it far ahead of other countries. Its fleet is more than three times the size of Russia’s and exceeds the combined totals of the next four countries in the ranking. Russia comes second with 4,237 military aircraft, followed by China with 3,529. India ranks fourth with 2,183, while South Korea occupies fifth place with 1,540. Pakistan follows with 1,429 aircraft, ahead of Japan, which has 1,397. Türkiye ranks eighth with 1,101, while Egypt has 1,088. France completes the top 10 with 974 military aircraft. The ranking includes aircraft across military branches, covering helicopters, transport planes, training aircraft and other military aviation assets, rather than combat jets alone. The United States’ substantial advantage reflects the requirements of maintaining military operations across multiple regions of the world. Its armed forces need to transport troops, equipment and supplies over long distances while supporting combat missions far from home bases. These operations depend on a broad aviation network that includes cargo aircraft, aerial refuelling tankers, helicopters and fighter jets. The ability to transport personnel and equipment and keep aircraft supplied with fuel is essential to sustaining military operations overseas. However, the difference between the United States and China becomes smaller when the comparison is restricted to fighter and interceptor aircraft. The United States has 1,791 fighters and interceptors, compared with China’s 1,443. This gives Washington an advantage of approximately 24 per cent in this category. The narrower gap demonstrates that the United States’ lead in total military aircraft is partly attributable to the size and diversity of its wider aviation fleet, rather than fighter aircraft alone. Naval Assets China has the world’s largest navy by the number of vessels in the Global Firepower ranking, with 841 naval assets. The United States follows with 465, while Russia ranks third with 343. The ranking reflects China’s expanding maritime capabilities and its extensive shipbuilding industry. Research by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) has examined how China’s commercial shipbuilding infrastructure can also support military ship production, providing an industrial foundation for expanding its naval fleet. North Korea ranks fourth with 338 naval assets, followed by Sweden with 332. Indonesia occupies sixth place with 304 vessels, while Italy ranks seventh with 285. India is eighth with 279 naval assets, Thailand ranks ninth with 275, and Sri Lanka completes the top 10 with 275 vessels. China’s total of 841 vessels is substantially higher than the United States’ 465, but vessel counts provide only one measure of naval strength. The figures include different types of vessels, ranging from small patrol boats and coastal craft to larger warships. Each vessel contributes one unit to the total, regardless of its size, armament or operational role. As a result, a country with numerous smaller vessels may rank above another whose fleet contains fewer but significantly larger and more capable ships. The ranking changes when naval strength is measured by total fleet tonnage instead of vessel numbers. Under Global Firepower’s fleet-tonnage ranking, the United States takes first place, with approximately 2.6 times China’s total displacement. Fleet tonnage measures the combined displacement of a navy’s vessels and provides a different perspective on the scale of its maritime assets. Nevertheless, tonnage also has limitations. It does not independently measure a vessel’s weapons, technological sophistication, operational readiness or combat effectiveness. Taken together, the rankings demonstrate why military strength cannot be assessed through a single measure. Personnel numbers reveal the size of a country’s active force, tank inventories highlight its armoured capabilities, aircraft totals reflect its aviation resources, and naval counts offer insight into its maritime presence. However, equipment quality, training, logistics, technology and the ability to deploy forces effectively are also crucial to determining a military’s overall strength. items.title: Sécurité numérique au Burkina : La BCLCC lance la 2ᵉ Semaine nationale de lutte contre la cybercriminalité
items.description: La Brigade centrale de lutte contre la cybercriminalité (BCLCC) organise la 2ᵉ Semaine nationale de lutte contre la cybercriminalité au Burkina Faso autour du thème « Cybercriminalité et menaces numériques émergentes : du clic au crime ». À cette occasion, plusieurs activités de sensibilisation, de formation et de coopération sont prévues à Ouagadougou et dans d’autres villes du pays. Les grandes articulations de cette édition ont été présentées le vendredi 23 octobre 2026, lors d’une conférence de presse à Ouagadougou. Pendant cinq jours, panels, sessions de formation en sécurité numérique, caravanes de sensibilisation et journées portes ouvertes rythmeront cette semaine consacrée à la lutte contre les infractions commises dans le cyberespace. Parmi les innovations annoncées figurent un Forum africain de l’éducation aux médias et à l’information, réunissant des acteurs du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger, ainsi qu’un hackathon consacré aux investigations numériques. Placée sous le thème « Investigations numériques : tracer l’invisible, certifier le réel, décrypter la preuve et réinventer l’investigation face au crime du moment », cette compétition entend mettre en avant les capacités d’innovation et la recherche de solutions technologiques face aux nouvelles formes de criminalité numérique. Organisée par la BCLCC, sous l’égide du ministère de la Sécurité, cette semaine s’inscrit dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de la stratégie nationale de lutte contre la cybercriminalité. Selon le Commandant de la BCLCC, le Commissaire Principal de Police Bayi Akim Nignan, cette édition se veut « un cadre d’information, de sensibilisation et d’action concertée ». Plus de 9 milliards de F CFA de préjudices en cinq ans « Nous voulons promouvoir une culture nationale de cyberprudence et de citoyenneté numérique responsable, à renforcer la coopération entre les acteurs de l’écosystème numérique et à encourager la conception de solutions technologiques locales contre la cybercriminalité », a déclaré le commandant de la BCLCC. Au-delà de la prévention, l’initiative ambitionne de « restaurer la confiance des citoyens dans les services numériques et financiers » et de « réduire les risques liés au blanchiment de capitaux et au financement du terrorisme par le numérique ». L’ampleur des préjudices enregistrés souligne l’importance de ces actions. Entre 2020 et 2025, la BCLCC a recensé des pertes financières estimées à plus de 9 milliards de FCFA, résultant de différentes formes d’escroqueries et d’infractions commises dans le cyberespace national. À ces infractions s’ajoutent d’autres menaces, notamment la désinformation, les hypertrucages, communément appelés deepfakes , les discours de haine et les appels à la violence sur les réseaux sociaux. Le développement des services financiers numériques constitue également un défi. « L’essor des cryptomonnaies, des plateformes d’investissement en ligne et des paris numériques constitue un terrain favorable aux escroqueries financières et au blanchiment de capitaux. Les fraudes liées au mobile money, au mobile banking et au commerce en ligne exposent par ailleurs les citoyens à des pertes financières » , a souligné Bayi Akim Nignan. Face à cette diversité de risques, le Commandant de la BCLCC estime que la lutte contre la cybercriminalité exige une adaptation permanente aux évolutions technologiques. items.title: Aurangzeb rules out consumption-led growth, says tariff reforms will continue
items.description: LAHORE: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb has ruled out pursuing liquidity-fuelled, consumption-led economic growth, saying Pakistan must prioritise sustainable, export-led expansion and continue with tariff reforms to improve the competitiveness of its industries. The finance minister was speaking at the Lahore University of Management Sciences (Lums) on Saturday at an event organised by the American Business Forum (ABF). ABF President Osman Khalid Waheed, former State Bank governor Raza Baqir and Habib Group Vice Chairman Salman Burni also spoke. Aurangzeb said Pakistan could not afford to repeat the cycle of import-dependent growth that had previously led to balance-of-payments problems and forced the country to seek support from lenders of last resort. He said the government was committed to continuing tariff reforms , primarily to reduce the cost of raw materials and intermediate goods for exporters, despite concerns over the timing of the measures. “We are very clear: no matter how much pressure there is, we are not going to go for liquidity-fuelled, consumption-led growth,” he said, adding that Pakistan needed to avoid another cycle in which a temporary acceleration in economic activity was followed by a balance-of-payments crisis. Aurangzeb said the government had attempted to provide a direction towards export-led growth in the latest budget through measures including the elimination of super taxes, reductions in tax slabs and financing for exporters at 4.5 per cent. On tariff reforms, he said the government had protected domestic industries for too long without sunset clauses and that the existing approach could not continue indefinitely. “We are in year two of the tariff reform, and we are going to continue with that; there is no turning back,” he said. The finance minister also stressed that economic growth needed to generate employment, pointing to the contrast between Pakistan’s growth trajectory and that of its neighbour, where growth of 7 to 8pc, he argued, had not translated into sufficient job creation. “That’s why you see people there where they are,” he said, emphasising that the sectors driving growth must also address unemployment. Global outlook remains uncertain Reflecting on discussions at international forums in New York, London and the annual meetings of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Bangkok, Aurangzeb said the global economy had remained resilient but faced an uncertain and worrying outlook. He identified growing differences in economic fortunes between oil-exporting and oil-importing countries, as well as economies benefiting from artificial intelligence, as key themes in discussions on global growth. Energy shocks and the El Nino weather phenomenon had featured prominently in discussions, he said, warning that their effects were intensifying and contributing to food-security concerns in some parts of the world. He also highlighted high debt levels, limited fiscal space in some economies and the growing importance of digital infrastructure and labour-market preparedness for artificial intelligence. As trade fragmentation and geopolitical polarisation intensified, regional corridors and regional blocs were emerging as significant opportunities, he said, adding that these developments could be particularly important for Pakistan. Twin deficits narrow The finance czar said Pakistan had made significant progress in reducing its fiscal and external imbalances, with the combined twin deficits falling from 12.5pc of gross domestic product (GDP) to 2.6pc by the end of the last fiscal year. He said the fiscal deficit had dropped to a 22-year low, while the country had recorded primary surpluses for three consecutive years. The current account deficit narrowed to around 0.1pc of GDP, supported by remittances and IT exports. Aurangzeb said IT export services had risen from less than $1 billion to $4.6bn and were projected to reach $5.5bn in the current fiscal year. Foreign exchange reserves had improved to over three months of import cover, compared with two weeks during the crisis. Citing three credit-rating upgrades since April last year, he said a recent Panda bond had attracted an order book twice its size, reflecting investor confidence beyond Pakistan’s current IMF programme, due to end in October next year. Conflict puts pressure on energy security He further said that Pakistan had managed immediate energy-supply challenges amid the continuing Middle East conflict , with supplies secured through November and arrangements for winter underway. He said the government had shifted from blanket subsidies to targeted support , citing the high cost of universal subsidies. Assuming an average household size of four to five people, the programme had reached an estimated 40 million to 50 million people, he said, adding that energy and gas supplies remained areas requiring attention. Debt management and access to finance The minister maintained that government borrowing had placed a disproportionate burden on the banking sector, but domestic debt-management operations had helped reduce debt-servicing costs to Rs6.9 trillion against a budgeted Rs8.2tr in the last fiscal year. He said external debt payments had declined from $26.5 billion last year to $21.5bn in the current fiscal year and were expected to fall further. New external borrowing was largely aimed at replacing existing obligations, rather than increasing the debt burden. Aurangzeb also highlighted pension reforms, saying new entrants to the civil bureaucracy had shifted from defined-benefit to defined-contribution schemes, while discussions with the armed forces were ongoing. Population, investment and inclusive growth The finance minister said the government has identified climate change and population growth as major challenges for Pakistan, urging measures to reduce the country’s 2.55pc population growth rate. He cited Bangladesh, Indonesia and Iran as examples, saying all three had reduced their population growth rates to below 1pc over a decade. He stressed women’s education, workforce participation and engagement with religious scholars as key measures. Aurangzeb said restoring investor confidence required macroeconomic stability and the clearance of around $4 billion in outstanding dividend and profit repatriation obligations. He also highlighted improving domestic investment, citing 11 initial public offerings last year — a 20-year high — and five in the current year. The finance minister said harmonising federal and provincial regulatory frameworks was essential to attract investment, as businesses often faced differing requirements at both levels. He stressed that reforms in taxation, energy and financing were necessary to sustain growth, improve export competitiveness and create jobs.

items.title: Which countries are best at maths? See top 10

The ranking compares the average mathematics scores of students across participating countries and economies. PISA assesses more than the ability to memorise formulas, examining how well students apply mathematical knowledge and reasoning to real-world problems. More than 760,000 students participated in PISA 2025 across 91 countries and economies, representing roughly 33 million 15-year-olds worldwide. Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse: Headmaster has no right to use accuser’s motherhood to justify alleged rape – NETRIGHT
items.description: Convener of the Network for Women’s Rights (NETRIGHT), Professor Akosua A. Adarkwa, says the suspended Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) headmaster Zakaria Abdulai has worsened his position by publicly referring to the age and parental status of the student who accused him of rape. She said his comments, in which he disclosed that the accuser was between 20 and 21 years old and had a child, raised further concerns about attitudes towards women and the justification of sexual abuse. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, Prof Adarkwa said the remarks suggested a troubling attitude towards female students and the circumstances in which they could be vulnerable to abuse. “But actually, he’s made his case worse because it means he’s sitting at the school and he’s trying to figure out which of these girls he should go and abuse. That’s what he’s saying to us,” she said. Prof Adarkwa stressed that a woman’s character or personal circumstances could never justify sexual assault, insisting that even if the student had a reputation for misconduct, that would not give the headmaster the right to abuse her. “And you, the headmaster, does that give you a right then? Even if she was the chief of the bad girls association, not just the Ghana version, international. She is the lead of the bad girls association international. Does that give you the right to sexually assault her? And then stand in public and use it as justification,” she asked. Read also: Obuasi SHTS headmaster says rape accuser is 20 to 21 years old and has a child She also criticised what she described as a lack of respect for women in Ghanaian society, arguing that the absence of strong public condemnation of such remarks could embolden people to express attitudes that excuse sexual violence. “Because part of this is also that we have no respect for women in this country. So, he can boldly say something like that. He doesn’t get a reaction that makes him think, ‘Wait a minute, maybe I shouldn’t, even if I’m thinking this, I shouldn’t have the nerve to open my mouth and say this,’” she said. Prof Adarkwa expressed concern about reactions to the case on social media, saying some comments appeared to trivialise the allegations or suggest that the student’s circumstances could be used to judge her credibility. She urged the public to reflect on the controversy and examine the social attitudes that allow the mistreatment of girls and women to be defended or normalised. “If you go on social media, you’ll be sick. Because sometimes I read and I’m wondering, is this person being contrarian just to have a laugh? Do they really, honestly, truly believe this? And if they do, how come we’ve created a society where we think it is acceptable to treat girls like this. We need to use this as a learning moment for all of us,” she added. Background Mr Abdulai, who has been suspended amid allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi SHTS, made the comments in an interview with radio host Blakk Rasta while responding to reports surrounding the case. “I know she’s given birth. She has a child. She’s 20 to 21 years. But I cannot judge her; whether she’s bad or good. I cannot. But I have my story,” he said. He also disclosed that he had been cautioned by the police following a complaint lodged by the student and her parents, and that he had been granted self-recognisance bail while awaiting court proceedings. “I have been cautioned because one girl and her parents said I have raped her. So, they reported, I was cautioned, and as a headmaster I was given self-recognisance bail. I’m waiting for court days,” he said. Mr Abdulai maintained that he had his own account of the events and said the committee that investigated the matter had heard both his account and that of the student and her relatives. The allegations remain subject to investigation, and the claims against the suspended headmaster have not been established in court.

items.title: Obuasi SHTS scandal: Investigate all schools where headmaster previously worked – Akosua Manu
items.description: The Adviser on Gender and Social Protection to former Vice-President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, Akosua Manu, has called for investigations into all schools where the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, previously worked, following allegations of sexual abuse involving female students. Her comments follow allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School, brought to public attention through investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni’s documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow. Appearing on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, Ms Manu said investigations should extend beyond the current allegations to examine how complaints were handled at the headmaster’s previous institutions and whether officials responsible for student protection fulfilled their duties. “Now, what I want us to do is to call for an investigation. Every school that he has been in, we have to look at everybody who was a safety protocol officer there,” she stated. She also demanded scrutiny of Ghana Education Service (GES) officials who may have received complaints but allegedly failed to take appropriate action. “We need to see who is in charge, even at GES, who receives these complaints and flips the paper over and says that it’s normal,” she added. Ms Manu expressed concern about the power imbalance between school authorities and students, particularly girls from economically disadvantaged backgrounds who depend on the Free Senior High School (Free SHS) policy to continue their education. According to her, some students may remain silent about sexual abuse for fear of losing their educational opportunities or facing retaliation from influential school authorities. “Now, when you go to school and this happens to you, do you not fear that you may not complete your education? So you’d rather keep quiet and finish school,” she said. She argued that such vulnerabilities could expose students to exploitation, especially where effective reporting and safeguarding systems are absent. The former adviser also questioned the institutional oversight that allowed the reported transfer of at least 38 teachers from the school without, in her view, sufficient scrutiny. “What audit process at GES says, ‘Hold up, how have 38 people been transferred from your institution in the last couple of years? What is going on?'” she questioned. Ms Manu further raised concerns about alleged attempts to influence complainants and their families, citing reports that some had been approached with offers of educational support in exchange for withdrawing complaints. She disclosed that, of the 19 girls reportedly linked to the allegations, only four had physically come forward to give accounts of their experiences, while one complainant had reportedly withdrawn her police complaint. She commended the efforts of a parent who reportedly involved the local Odikro to document an alleged attempt to persuade the family to abandon its complaint. Ms Manu also criticised attempts to discredit alleged victims through claims about their personal backgrounds, insisting that such narratives could never justify sexual abuse. “It doesn’t matter. You do not have a right to abuse her,” she stressed. Turning to the political controversy surrounding the allegations, she criticised the handling of the matter by the National Democratic Congress (NDC), questioning its reported decision to clear the headmaster to contest a party position before subsequently changing its stance following public criticism. She argued that political considerations should not overshadow the protection of children or the need for accountability. Ms Manu also called for stronger institutional safeguards, stressing that school authorities, education officials and law enforcement agencies must be held accountable where investigations establish failures in their responsibilities.

items.title: Suspect accused of assaulting female scooty rider in Lahore granted bail
items.description: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Saturday granted post-arrest bail to a man accused of assaulting a woman riding a scooty on Mozang Ring Road. Police had arrested the suspect after CCTV footage of the incident, which took place on Thursday, sparked widespread public outrage on social media. The man was tracked down with the help of data from dozens of Punjab Safe Cities Authority (PSCA) cameras and jailed after being nominated in a criminal case. On Saturday, Mozang police presented the suspect before the court and requested that he be sent to jail on judicial remand as his physical remand was not required. However, the magistrate, under his powers, ordered the suspect’s release on bail against a surety bond of Rs100,000, if he was not required in any other criminal case. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif took to X to express her displeasure at the suspect receiving bail, posting multiple screenshots of TV news reports about the case and writing “sad” in all caps. In a post two hours earlier, Maryam said she had spoken to the girl and told her “she should slap the man as many times as he had slapped her”. “But she said that, for her, it was enough that the government had made her feel protected, cared for, and assured that justice was on her side,” she said. The footage showed that a man overtook the female scooty rider on the busy road, placed his bike in front of her two-wheeler, and allegedly subjected her to brutal torture in the presence of several passersby. None of the onlookers seemingly tried to intervene and rescue the woman as the suspect pulled her hair and slapped her repeatedly. As per initial police reports, the woman suffered facial injuries, including a nasal bone fracture, during the attack. A police official said the attacker also threw the victim’s bag on the ground that contained a laptop valued at around Rs90,000, resulting in severe damage. The suspect later fled the scene in the presence of several onlookers, he added. In April this year, CM Maryam ordered Lahore police to arrest a suspect who allegedly snatched a phone from a girl riding a scooty in Nawab Town and injured her when she put up resistance. A video clip showed the suspect dragging her on the road, fleeing the scene with her mobile phone. The girl, 17, suffered multiple bruises and injuries to her legs and arms. She was riding the scooty outside her home when the unidentified man snatched her phone.

items.title: Coopération: le ministre de la Sécurité reçoit une délégation de l’UICN
items.description: Le ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou SANA, a reçu en audience, ce vendredi 23 octobre 2026, à son cabinet, une délégation de l’Union internationale pour la conservation de la nature (UICN), conduite par Balla Moussa SIDIBE, directeur régional du Programme Afrique occidentale et centrale. Les échanges ont porté sur la présentation des missions de l’UICN, le bilan des initiatives menées en collaboration avec les structures nationales, ainsi que les perspectives de coopération avec le ministère de la Sécurité. « Nous sortons confiants et rassurés, car le ministre de la Sécurité a une vision très claire de ce partenariat, tant au Burkina Faso qu’à l’échelle régionale. Nous sommes convaincus que nous allons pouvoir réaliser beaucoup de choses ici, de manière très concrète et pragmatique », a souligné le directeur régional, Balla Moussa SIDIBE. Présente au Burkina Faso depuis plusieurs décennies, l’UICN intervient notamment dans la conservation de la biodiversité, la gestion durable des ressources naturelles et la restauration des terres. Elle contribue également au renforcement de la résilience des communautés face aux changements environnementaux et climatiques. Pour sa part, le ministre de la Sécurité a salué les actions menées par l’UICN au Burkina Faso depuis 1991. Il a réaffirmé la disponibilité de son département à accompagner les initiatives de l’organisation en matière de conservation de la nature au Burkina Faso. items.title: FIFA: Infantino says backed by ‘vast majority’ in bid for re-election
items.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has said he has the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of member associations in his bid for re-election despite criticism of his aborted World Cup selloff plan. The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) rallied behind Infantino on Friday in a significant boost to the 56-year-old’s hopes of winning a fourth term in charge. Infantino’s future in the role was in doubt two months ago when he faced a furious backlash to his plan to sell off a portion of the commercial rights of competitions run by football’s world governing body to private investors. The heads of European football’s governing body UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF, which runs the game in North and Central America, signed a letter saying football “belongs to no individual”. But Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed private investment project, is now in a strong position to secure re-election in March. “I think what is important is that in an organisation like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view,” Infantino told the BBC on Saturday. “But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone, if we are serious about that, then we need to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority. “I’m just coming back off Tokyo where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde where all African countries have endorsed me. I’m speaking to all associations everywhere in the world.” No other candidate has yet come forward to oppose Infantino with the deadline to do so less than a month away on November 18. He added: “There are different points of view it’s not always easy to bring them all under one roof but we need to respect and I do respect all opinions all views and then it will be up to the FIFA member associations to decide who they want as a president and how they want FIFA to be run.” The post FIFA: Infantino says backed by ‘vast majority’ in bid for re-election appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le poème du dimanche | ‘‘Ceci n’est pas un poème’’ de Arwa Ben Dhia
items.description: Arwa Ben Dhia est docteure en électronique, ingénieure brevets et autrice tunisienne polyglotte, elle a publié plusieurs recueils de poésie. Née en Tunisie en 1986 et installée en France depuis 2009, elle a remporté plusieurs prix littéraires. Traductrice, elle a dirigé une anthologie poétique, ‘‘ Nos muses les murs’’ , Ed. Mindset, 2025. Honorée par la distinction d’Ambassadrice de la Paiix, attribuée par le Cercle Universel des Ambassadeurs de la Paix (CUAP). Tahar Bekri Aucune image. Ceci n'est pas un poème. Ni rime, ni prosodie. Ceci n'est pas un poème. Cessez les devinettes. Ne comptez pas les syllabes. Ne cherchez pas les erreurs. Ceci n'est pas un poème. Sans inspiration. Sans raison. Ceci n'est pas un poème. Nulle farce. Nulle offense. Ceci n'est pas un poème. Soyez indulgents. Peut-être êtes-vous le poème. items.title: L’eau, ce casse-tête dans nos territoires (Par Maguette NDONG)
items.description: La volonté des autorités de permettre à chaque citoyen de disposer d’une eau potable est manifeste. Avant-hier, lors de l’atelier national préparatoire de la Conférence des Nations Unies sur l’eau d’Abu d’Abi en décembre prochain, le ministre de l'hydraulique et de l'Assainissement, Cheikh Tidiane Dieye avait évalué les besoins du pays à 2631 milliards de Fcfa pour la période 2026-2030. Seulement, il n'avait pas manqué de préciser que le défi principal était de convertir « les priorités en réalisations concrètes » et inscrire l’eau au plus haut niveau de l’agenda économique et financier du gouvernement. Plus concrètement, il y a encore des milliers de villages au Sénégal qui ne disposent pas d’eau potable. Ce qui compromet la santé et l'hygiène de leurs habitants au fil des années. Dans la région de Dakar, dans une commune comme Tivaouane-Peulh Niague, plusieurs quartiers sont encore privés d’eau potable, les empêchant de satisfaire leurs besoins journaliers. Pour en disposer, des mères de famille se rabattent sur les quelques puits creusés par des organisations caritatives d'obédience islamique ou chrétienne comme Caritas. Les plus nantis de ces chefs de famille se voient obliger de creuser des pompes artisanales, sans que la qualité ou la potabilité de l’eau ne soit garantie. Malgré les efforts de l’État, l’eau reste encore un casse-tête pour de nombreux dakarois. Or, la recommandation générale faite par l’Organisation mondiale de la Santé est que chaque adulte doit boire 2 litres par jour ; ce nombre de litre est de quatre pour les personnes exerçant des activités physiques ou habitant dans un climat chaud. De même, les enfants doivent boire 2 litres d’eau par jour. D’ailleurs, dans l’Odd 6 des Nations-Unies, il a été clairement indiqué que l’accès à l’eau potable, à l’assainissement et à l’hygiène est le besoin humain le plus fondamental pour la santé et le bien-être. Aussi, en 2022, 2,2 milliards de personnes dans le monde ne disposaient toujours pas d’eau potable gérée en toute sécurité, dont 703 millions sans service d’eau de base. Il faut dire que le stress hydrique touche la plupart des continents du monde, principalement en Afrique et en Asie. Au Sénégal, ce manque d’eau est souvent résorbé par la multiplication des branchements sociaux un peu partout. Tandis que l’Office des forages ruraux (Ofor) signe des contrats d’affermage pour que le monde rural ne sente pas exclu de cet effort. En plus de cela, certains maires et élus locaux font de l’accès à l’eau une priorité. Au point que beaucoup d’entre eux ont élargi leur réseau d’adduction en eau à différentes localités ou villages de leur circonscription. Récemment, le président du Conseil départemental de Louga, Amadou Mberry Sylla a dégagé une enveloppe de 50 millions de FCfa pour donner de l’eau aux populations qui n’en avaient pas. À Khombole, le maire Maguèye Boye a pris le taureau par les cornes pour élargir le réseau de la commune. Récemment, le maire de Djinaky à Bignona a promis d’injecter 100 millions de FCfa, sur fonds propres pour permettre à ses concitoyens de disposer du liquide précieux. On le voit bien, les efforts pour satisfaire les besoins en eau des populations sont devenus une préoccupation aussi bien de l’État que des élus locaux ainsi que des organisations de la société civile. Toutefois, l’eau manque encore à quelques kilomètres de la capitale sénégalaise. L’exemple de Tivaouane Peulh est évocateur. Il est donc plus que jamais temps que les promesses se traduisent en réalisations concrètes. maguette.ndong@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Pakistan rejects ex-US envoy Khalilzad’s 'baseless' allegations of arming Afghans to fight Taliban
items.description: The information ministry on Saturday rejected former United States envoy Zalmay Khalilzad’s “baseless and misleading allegations” that Pakistan was “arming Afghans to fight the Taliban”. The ministry’s response came a day after Khalilzad, who served as special representative to Afghanistan during the first Trump administration, claimed on X that there were “ many reports that Pakistan is arming Afghans to fight the Taliban in Afghanistan”. He further alleged that Pakistan was now “recruiting Afghans to fight against anti-Pakistan insurgents”, adding that ties between the two countries were likely to “get much worse”. “His sweeping baseless assertions merely recycle speculative narratives as part of his personal agenda to prop [the] terrorism-supporting Taliban regime,” the information ministry’s fact-check account said on X. It rebuked Khalilzad, saying his “[peddling] of such unsubstantiated allegations only exposes his skewed agenda-based views”. The ministry highlighted that it was “particularly misleading to conflate Pakistan’s legitimate counterterrorism operations against terrorist organisations operating from inside Afghan Taliban regime-controlled areas threatening its citizens with allegations of recruiting Afghan nationals or sponsoring armed groups inside Afghanistan”. “Pakistan remains at the forefront of the fight against terrorism and has made enormous sacrifices in protecting regional peace and security,” it emphasised. It went on to point out that successive monitoring reports issued by the United Nations had documented the continued presence and activities of terrorist organisations, including the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and Al-Qaeda, inside Afghanistan. “Khalilzad’s allegations conveniently divert attention from the Afghan Taliban regime’s responsibility to prevent its territory from being used by India-sponsored proxies for terrorism against Pakistan,” the statement added. Khalilzad, who negotiated a US deal with the Taliban that led to the withdrawal of Nato forces from Afghanistan, has previously called for Islamabad and Kabul to enter a negotiated settlement multiple times , as recently as January this year . In November last year, the information ministry criticised Khalilzad for “creating a false impression” of the militant group Islamic State-Khorasan (IS-K) having a presence in Punjab. The ex-US envoy had claimed an IS-K commander was killed in Punjab’s Akhtarabad. The ministry later clarified that a man had been killed during a dacoity/robbery-related incident, not a counterterrorism operation, and that there was no evidence linking him to IS-K. In March 2023, the Foreign Office (FO) reacted strongly to a series of suggestions made by Khalilzad, saying Pakistan did not need “unsolicited advice” on the challenges it faces. That statement by Khalilzad also prompted the US State Department to clarify that the former envoy did not represent the country’s foreign policy and did not speak for the administration of then-president Joe Biden. Ties between Pakistan and Afghanistan have been strained in the past few years as Islamabad continues to voice its concern over cross-border terrorism. September witnessed another bout of conflict between the two neighbours, with Pakistan carrying out calibrated airstrikes in the border region in response to terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. This was followed by drone incursions from across the border, which Islamabad said were shot down, and two further rounds of retaliatory airstrikes.

items.title: Électrification rurale : l’Aser a besoin de 400 milliards de FCFA pour raccorder 6 400 localités
items.description: L’Agence sénégalaise d’électrification rurale (Aser) estime à plus de 400 milliards de FCFA le financement nécessaire pour électrifier 6 400 localités encore non raccordées, en plus des 6 000 localités où les travaux sont déjà en cours. L’objectif de l’État est d’assurer l’accès universel à l’électricité à l’horizon 2029. Après Saint-Louis, le directeur général de l’Agence sénégalaise d’électrification rurale (Aser), Pape Momar Ngom, a poursuivi, vendredi, sa tournée dans la région de Louga, notamment dans le département de Kébémer. Il s’est rendu dans la commune de Kanène Ndiob, précisément à Darou Cissé, ainsi qu’à Thiss Wolof et Thiss Peul, des localités récemment raccordées au réseau électrique. À cette occasion, Pape Momar Ngom a réaffirmé l’ambition de l’État d’assurer l’accès universel à l’électricité à l’horizon 2029. Selon lui, 6 400 localités restent à électrifier, en plus des 6 000 localités dans lesquelles les travaux sont déjà en cours. « Il faut un financement de plus de 400 milliards de FCFA pour électrifier l’ensemble de ces villages. Nous sommes en train de travailler là-dessus, car cela demande beaucoup de moyens », a-t-il déclaré. Le directeur général de l’Aser a également fait état de promesses de financement de la part de partenaires privés. Il a précisé que les chantiers seront lancés dès la signature des contrats et des conventions de financement. Pour lui, l’accès à l’électricité constitue une condition essentielle du développement. « Sans électricité, on ne peut pas parler de développement », a-t-il soutenu. Évaluer les réalisations et écouter les populations La tournée du directeur général vise également à visiter les localités récemment raccordées afin d’évaluer le niveau de satisfaction des populations quant aux travaux réalisés. Elle doit aussi permettre de recueillir leurs préoccupations et leurs attentes, en vue d’identifier les interventions complémentaires que l’Aser pourrait mener, en collaboration avec la Compagnie maroco-sénégalaise de l’électricité (Comasel). Falel PAM

items.title: France : Nouvelle journée de mobilisation sous haute surveillance policière
items.description: Une semaine après les événements du 17 octobre, la France connaît ce samedi 24 octobre 2026 une nouvelle journée de mobilisation contre la vie chère. À la suite des violences et des pillages enregistrés lors des précédentes manifestations, les autorités ont renforcé le dispositif sécuritaire afin de prévenir de nouveaux débordements. Dans cette dynamique, le ministre de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, a annoncé la mobilisation de 70 000 policiers et gendarmes sur l'ensemble du territoire national. Une attention particulière est accordée à la ville d'Orléans, où doit se tenir un congrès du Rassemblement national (RN) dans un contexte de fortes tensions. Par ailleurs, plusieurs manifestations ont été interdites dans des villes comme Paris, Bordeaux et Rennes. Ces mesures visent à prévenir de nouveaux actes de vandalisme et de pillage, ainsi que d'éventuels affrontements entre manifestants et forces de l'ordre. Selon un bilan provisoire du ministère de l'Intérieur, 135 personnes ont été interpellées et 136 actions sur la voie publique ont été recensées. Au total, 35 000 personnes ont été dénombrées dans l'espace public dans le cadre de cette journée de mobilisation. Alors que les mobilisations se poursuivent ce samedi, les Gilets jaunes appellent déjà à une nouvelle journée de protestation, prévue le 31 octobre 2026, pour « la défense des libertés publiques ». Des rassemblements et des sit-in sont annoncés devant l'Assemblée nationale et les mairies afin de dénoncer ce qu'ils qualifient de « dérive autoritaire » du gouvernement. Lire aussi : Manifestations contre la vie chère : La France dans le chaos ce samedi Minute.bf

items.title: Les pêcheurs tunisiens de la crevette rouge regardent vers l’Italie
items.description: «Rome décidera-t-elle de l’avenir de la pêche à la crevette rouge en Méditerranée ?», s’est demandé l’ancien député Majdi Karbai, résident en Italie, en évoquant, dans un poste Facebook, la 49ᵉ session de la Commission générale des pêches pour la Méditerranée (CGPM), qui se tiendra du 26 au 30 octobre 2026, au siège de l’Organisation des Nations unies pour l’alimentation et l’agriculture (FAO), à Rome, avec la participation de plusieurs pays, dont la Tunisie et l’Italie qu’oppose un litige commercial à ce sujet. Les raisons de l’abondance de crevettes sur le marché tunisien Cette réunion intervient dans un contexte sensible, après le dépassement du quota tunisien de pêche à la crevette rouge en 2026, selon des informations relayées par la presse, et les pressions qui en ont résulté sur les exportateurs tunisiens et importateurs italien, a fait remarquer Karbai, et de préciser que «l’enjeu n’est pas seulement environnemental : il est aussi économique et politique.» «Qui fixe les quotas de pêche ? Sur quels critères ? Les règles sont-elles appliquées équitablement à tous les pays, ou la durabilité devient-elle un instrument de pression sur les pêcheurs et les produits tunisiens ?» , s’interroge-t-il, faisant ainsi écho aux requêtes des pêcheurs tunisiens de crevette rouge qui se considèrent lésés par les quotas qui leur sont attribués par l’Italie et l’Union européenne. Et il répond : «Entre la préservation des ressources marines et la défense des intérêts des pêcheurs, une question demeure : les décisions prises à Rome seront-elles équitables et transparentes, ou les pêcheurs tunisiens paieront-ils le prix des rapports de force en Méditerranée ?» Sans attendre les conclusions officielles de la réunion, on peut compter sur les responsables tunisiens pour défendre les intérêts de leurs pêcheurs avec force argument, mais rien ne laisse présager une issue positive pour ces derniers qui devraient chercher d’autres débouchés pour leurs produits et ne pas dépendre d’un seul marché, en l’occurrence européen. I. B. L’article Les pêcheurs tunisiens de la crevette rouge regardent vers l’Italie est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Alake’s attack on Atiku won’t cut food prices, ADC campaign fires back
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council has fired back at Information Minister Dele Alake over his allegations against former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, saying no amount of political propaganda can shield President Bola Tinubu’s administration from public anger over rising living costs. The council argued that Nigerians were more concerned about the cost of food, fuel and transportation than allegations of artificial intelligence manipulation and deepfakes, challenging Alake to produce evidence linking Atiku or the ADC to the alleged fabricated letter and video. In a statement on Saturday, Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, described Alake’s intervention as an attempt to divert attention from the government’s record, insisting that the economic hardship confronting Nigerians was real and undeniable. “Until then, his ‘fake news alert’ is an empty political stunt,” Shaibu said, challenging the minister to provide names, dates and forensic findings to substantiate his allegations. Citing petrol prices of about ₦1,400 per litre, diesel prices above ₦2,000 and food inflation hovering around 20 per cent, Shaibu said the economic pressures facing households could not be dismissed as fabricated information. The council also cited a World Bank poverty estimate reported by Reuters, arguing that the administration’s economic direction had left millions of Nigerians struggling to make ends meet. Turning to Tinubu’s campaign rally in Kaduna, Shaibu questioned the explanation that a vehicle seen near an APC billboard was on routine patrol, asking why a campaign billboard required such protection. He also raised concerns over reports that supporters had travelled from distant states and were left sleeping on Kaduna’s streets. The statement further referred to reports of accidents involving APC supporters travelling from Sokoto and Abuja to the rally, although details remained unconfirmed. Shaibu urged the APC to account for the safety of those travelling to its campaign events, condemning what he described as the exploitation of supporters for political optics. “Making citizens endure long, hazardous journeys and sleep outdoors simply to create rally optics is political exploitation, not leadership,” he said. The ADC campaign council also questioned Tinubu’s reported decision to campaign in only 12 states, alleging that supporters were being moved from one rally to another to project an impression of widespread popular backing. “You can hire buses, assemble a crowd and plaster the streets with billboards. You cannot hire consent,” Shaibu said. He maintained that the APC’s economic record, rather than its attacks on the opposition, would shape its electoral prospects, insisting that Nigerians enduring high prices and shrinking incomes would ultimately judge the administration at the polls. “Alake’s attack on Atiku will not reduce the cost of a meal by one naira,” Shaibu added. The council expressed confidence that voters would reject the APC, promising a different economic direction under Atiku. “Bola made life expensive; Atiku will make Nigeria affordable again!” Shaibu declared. items.title: Obuasi SHTS scandal: State has failed alleged victims – Akosua Manu
items.description: The Adviser on Gender and Social Protection to former Vice-President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, Akosua Manu, has criticised state institutions over what she describes as their failure to adequately protect female students allegedly sexually abused by the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School. Her comments follow allegations involving 19 female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School, brought to public attention through Manasseh Azure Awuni’s investigative documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, Ms Manu said the Ghana Education Service (GES), Ministry of Education and Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection should have taken immediate steps to identify and protect the alleged victims, preserve evidence and prevent further abuse. She stressed that although the headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, is entitled to due process and the presumption of innocence, authorities do not need to wait for a criminal conviction before implementing measures to safeguard students. “First of all, Zakaria and whatever due process he’s entitled to is the law. He should experience it, no problem,” she stated. “Now, protective measures do not require a criminal conviction. I’m saying this because Zakaria does not need to go to court to be found guilty before the state, from GES, Ministry of Education, Gender Ministry, for them to trace the victims,” she added. Ms Manu argued that the response of state institutions had been inadequate, particularly following the allegations and accounts presented in investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni’s documentary. “And this is where I believe the state failed, especially in light of the overwhelming evidence that has been presented in the last week,” she said. She also expressed concern about reports of individuals allegedly approaching families of complainants, stressing the need for authorities to protect potential witnesses and preserve relevant evidence. According to her, the controversy should not be reduced to political disagreements, as the welfare of the affected students must remain the priority. “I’m going to focus on the girls, and it’s important that we do. Because it goes beyond the politics at this point,” she emphasised. Highlighting the global prevalence of sexual violence, Ms Manu cited UNICEF’s 2024 estimates indicating that more than 370 million girls and women alive today experienced rape or sexual assault before the age of 18, representing approximately one in eight. She noted that the global estimate rises to about 650 million when non-contact forms of sexual violence are included, while approximately 79 million girls and women in sub-Saharan Africa have experienced contact sexual violence during childhood. Ms Manu further raised concerns about the unequal power relationship between teachers and students, arguing that some girls may feel compelled to comply with inappropriate demands because of fears about punishment or their academic performance. “What does this tell you? It tells you there is a certain power dynamic as far as the school is concerned,” she said. She warned that sexual abuse could have lifelong psychological consequences, including trauma and school dropout, particularly where effective protective measures are absent. The former adviser also questioned why media interviews with the headmaster had not sufficiently examined whether similar allegations had arisen during his previous postings at Juaben, Toase and Nsawam. She disclosed that a woman who had previously attended school at Juaben sent her a private message alleging that the headmaster had made inappropriate advances towards her and treated her harshly after she rejected them. “Once he makes advances towards you and you decline, you are dead. He will hit you with passion. He hated me so much, and I hated him back and avoided him like the plague,” Ms Manu quoted the woman as saying. She further relayed the woman’s claim that the number of potential complainants at Juaben could exceed 100, although that allegation has not been independently established. Ms Manu criticised sections of the media for what she described as insensitive reporting on sexual abuse, warning that sensational coverage could discourage victims and their families from seeking justice. Ms Manu maintained that protecting students, supporting complainants and ensuring a thorough investigation must take precedence over political considerations, while respecting the legal rights of everyone involved.

items.title: Maroc : 195 millions de dirhams attendus des paris et des jeux de hasard en 2027
items.description: Le projet de loi de finances 2027 prévoit 195 millions de dirhams de recettes issues des prélèvements sur les paris, des produits de la loterie et des bénéfices de la Société royale d’encouragement du cheval. En parallèle, le gouvernement propose de renforcer le contrôle fiscal des gains aux jeux de hasard, en permettant notamment le recours à la procédure de taxation d’office en cas de manquement aux obligations déclaratives. Le gouvernement marocain prévoit de mobiliser 195 millions de dirhams en 2027 à travers plusieurs ressources liées aux paris et aux jeux de hasard. Les estimations figurent dans le projet de loi de finances (PLF) 2027 et concernent les prélèvements sur les paris mutuels, les produits de la loterie ainsi que les bénéfices que la Société royale d’encouragement du cheval devrait reverser à l’État. Dans le détail, 90 millions de dirhams sont attendus des prélèvements sur les paris mutuels, tandis que les produits de la loterie devraient générer 80 millions de dirhams. À ces montants s’ajoutent 25 millions de dirhams correspondant aux bénéfices attendus de la Société royale d’encouragement du cheval. Ces trois postes totalisent ainsi 195 millions de dirhams. Il ne s’agit toutefois pas du chiffre d’affaires global du secteur des paris et des jeux de hasard au Maroc, ni de l’ensemble des recettes fiscales susceptibles d’en découler. 170 millions de dirhams affectés à des comptes spéciaux Sur les 195 millions de dirhams prévus, 170 millions devraient alimenter deux comptes spéciaux du Trésor. Le premier, consacré aux prélèvements sur les paris mutuels, devrait recevoir 90 millions de dirhams. Le second, lié aux produits de la loterie, bénéficierait de 80 millions de dirhams. Les dépenses autorisées pour chacun de ces comptes sont fixées à hauteur des recettes attendues, soit respectivement 90 et 80 millions de dirhams. Ces ressources sont donc destinées à financer les dépenses relevant des objectifs spécifiques de ces comptes, plutôt qu’à être intégrées indistinctement aux recettes générales du budget de l’État. Les 25 millions de dirhams restants correspondent aux bénéfices que la Société royale d’encouragement du cheval devrait distribuer à l’État. Cette somme figure parmi les recettes attendues des entreprises et organismes relevant du périmètre suivi par la Direction des entreprises publiques et de la privatisation. Le PLF maintient également deux autres rubriques relatives aux prélèvements sur les produits des jeux de hasard et sur les paris hippiques et les courses de lévriers. Aucun montant prévisionnel n’est cependant indiqué pour ces postes dans les tableaux concernés. Les 195 millions de dirhams ne constituent donc pas une estimation exhaustive de toutes les recettes publiques liées à ces activités. Les gains aux jeux de hasard davantage surveillés par le fisc Au-delà des recettes attendues, le projet de loi de finances prévoit un renforcement du contrôle fiscal des gains issus des jeux de hasard. La mesure proposée repose sur une modification de l’article 228 du Code général des impôts, relatif à la procédure de taxation d’office. Le dispositif vise à inclure les déclarations concernant les gains aux jeux de hasard, prévues par l’article 154 ter du Code général des impôts, parmi les situations susceptibles de justifier le recours à cette procédure. Concrètement, l’absence de dépôt d’une déclaration dans les délais légaux, ou le dépôt d’une déclaration incomplète, pourrait permettre à l’administration fiscale d’engager une procédure de taxation d’office, dans les conditions prévues par la législation en vigueur. Cette évolution vise à renforcer le respect des obligations déclaratives et à permettre à la Direction générale des impôts d’intervenir lorsque les contribuables concernés ne déclarent pas correctement les gains soumis à l’impôt. Il ne s’agit pas, à travers cette seule modification, de créer un nouvel impôt sur les jeux de hasard, mais d’élargir le champ d’application d’une procédure fiscale déjà existante. Une entrée en vigueur prévue au 1er janvier 2027 Selon le projet de loi, les modifications proposées concernant l’article 228 devraient entrer en vigueur le 1er janvier 2027, pour les procédures engagées à partir de cette date, sous réserve de l’adoption définitive du texte. Le dispositif prévoit donc un renforcement du suivi fiscal des gains aux jeux de hasard, tout en maintenant l’application des garanties et des règles de procédure prévues par la législation. Cette orientation traduit une double approche : d’une part, la mobilisation des recettes provenant des paris, de la loterie et des organismes liés aux courses hippiques ; d’autre part, le renforcement du contrôle des gains individuels soumis à des obligations fiscales. Des recettes limitées à l’échelle du budget de l’État Les 195 millions de dirhams programmés représentent une part réduite des ressources publiques prévues pour 2027. À titre de comparaison, les recettes ordinaires du budget général sont estimées à environ 482,4 milliards de dirhams dans le projet de loi de finances. Le montant de 195 millions équivaut ainsi à environ 0,04 % de cette estimation. Cette comparaison doit toutefois être interprétée avec prudence, puisque la majeure partie des recettes liées aux paris et à la loterie est destinée à des comptes spéciaux du Trésor et non directement intégrée aux recettes ordinaires du budget général. Ces prévisions illustrent la volonté de l’État de maintenir plusieurs sources de financement, tout en renforçant les mécanismes de contrôle fiscal applicables aux revenus issus des jeux de hasard. Les montants et les dispositions présentés restent néanmoins susceptibles d’évoluer au cours de l’examen parlementaire du projet de loi de finances 2027. items.title: Viimsanté : Une application mobile au service de la santé
items.description: L’application mobile Viimsanté a été officiellement lancée le vendredi 23 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Conçue pour simplifier le parcours de soins, cette solution numérique vise à faciliter la gestion des ordonnances médicales, à améliorer les échanges entre les acteurs de la santé et à renforcer la transparence dans la prise en charge des patients. Viimsanté est une application mobile conçue pour dématérialiser les procédures liées aux ordonnances médicales et réduire progressivement le recours au format papier. Elle est le fruit de l’expertise de deux professionnels burkinabè que le Dr Josué Delma, pharmacien et expert en systèmes de santé, et le Dr Nestor Sam, médecin expert en santé digitale et en stratégies de santé. La solution vise à faciliter la gestion des ordonnances médicales et à simplifier les interactions entre les professionnels de santé. Elle entend également renforcer les liens entre les prestations de soins et les mécanismes de prise en charge par les assurances maladie. Grâce à cette plateforme, les patients, les pharmaciens, les prescripteurs et les assureurs pourront se connecter directement depuis leurs téléphones portables. L’objectif est de rendre les démarches plus simples et d’améliorer le suivi des prescriptions ainsi que la coordination entre les différents acteurs. « Le lancement officiel de l’application a pour ambition de continuer un parcours de soin plus simple, plus fluide et plus transparent. Pour les patients, elle vise à faciliter les démarches de santé et des échanges. Pour les médecins et les pharmaciens, elle va faciliter certaines opérations et améliorer le suivi des prescriptions. Pour les assureurs, elle ambitionne de renforcer la traçabilité, la transparence et la coordination des échanges » , a affirmé le Dr Nestor Sam. Une initiative saluée par le ministère de la Santé Représentant le ministre de la Santé, le conseiller technique Pacédou Saré a salué l’engagement des promoteurs de cette plateforme. Selon lui, cette initiative s’inscrit dans la vision du camarade capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, qui accorde une place importante aux solutions technologiques répondant aux besoins concrets des populations. « La technologie n’est pas une fin en soi, sa valeur se mesure au problème concret qu’elle permet de résoudre et au bénéfice qu’elle apporte aux populations », a-t-il déclaré. Avec Viimsanté, les promoteurs entendent contribuer à la modernisation du système de santé burkinabè à travers le numérique. L’application ambitionne de faciliter les démarches des patients, d’améliorer le suivi des prescriptions et de renforcer la transparence des échanges entre les acteurs du secteur. Viimsanté est disponible gratuitement sur le Play Store, permettant ainsi aux citoyens de la télécharger sur leurs téléphones compatibles.
